_doc: The iso grammar of the village POC, read by scripts/iso/*.py and by components/village/iso/*. One source: nothing here is copied anywhere else. Grid: gx grows to screen right-down, gy to screen left-down, z up, one unit = one cell edge. Blender: x = gx, y = -gy, z = z. Camera orthographic, rotation (60, 0, 45) degrees, looking along (-0.612, 0.612, -0.5): the front of the scene is large gx + gy.
cellToScreen: screen.x = (gx - gy) * S / 2, screen.y = (gx + gy) * S / 4; the point is the grid corner (gx, gy) at ground level, relative to the corner (0, 0)

moon._doc: The one light, fixed for good: azimuth 225 deg, elevation 55 deg. L points toward the moon, in Blender coordinates. It comes from screen left: the visible -y face (grid +gy, screen left) is lit (n.L 0.41), the visible +x face (screen right) is in shadow, the top is lightest (n.L 0.82). A pole's shadow runs toward screen right, about 0.70 x its height on screen.

tones._doc: Three tones per material, chosen by n.L: top if n.L >= top, lit if n.L > lit, shadow otherwise, or if the pixel is occluded (direct light < occludedRatio x n.L).

_lineThickness: Ink on tier_6's houses is about 2 px on buildings about 150 px wide, so about 10 px at our 768 px; 8 keeps the small parts (anvil, hood posts) from drowning.

materials._doc: Three already-lit values per material [top, lit, shadow], final colours: the preamble asks FLUX to keep them as they are. Pipetted on the tier 1-7 buildings (2026-10-28), never on the sky or tier_6's cold windows; the source is beside each.

emissive._doc: Warm sources: flat, never shaded, never shadowed, and they cast no shadow.
emissive._ember: A banked bed of coals, darker and smaller than `fire`: the v5 probe's first attempt read the bright orange square as a lamp and lit the wall beside it on 8 renders out of 8.

pools._doc: A window's light pool: the window quad projected onto the ground from a lamp F inside, lampInset behind the face and lampAbove its top edge. Only vertical emissive faces facing -y or +x, whose bottom edge is below maxSill.

vieParAmbiance._doc: What the app draws by ambiance, beyond the painted images: the fireflies, the hearths' flames and their warm glow. Only `nuit` has any of it but two: `animaux` (the small animals walk a little in a wave) lives by day and by night. `oiseaux` is the birds that land on a roof: day only (audit T43 round 1, no bird at night). `jour` is allowed and draws only those two until a day exists (§7 of the V1 prompt). Read by Lucioles, Feux, the walkers' plan and the roof birds through isoSpec.ts `vieDe`.

ambiances._doc: Palettes and light, by ambiance (§7 of the V1 prompt). V1 fills `nuit` only; `jour` is an allowed name, absent until it is painted. Each field names the top-level block that holds it: scripts/iso/*.py read moon, tones, materials, emissive and pools at the top level, so nuit's values stay there instead of being copied. When `jour` arrives, move nuit's blocks in here and teach isolib.py to read them. Constraint on every ambiance's light: azimuth 225 deg and elevation 55 deg or higher. The master grid's spacing rule (constants/isoLayout.json) is built for shadows that fall toward +gx and -gy and reach no further than heights.json says; another azimuth or a lower light breaks it. __tests__/iso-layout.test.ts runs the spacing rule under every light listed here (a named block or an inline { azimuthDeg, elevationDeg }) and turns red on one that breaks it.

biomes._doc: Ground colours, decor, water and the world around the island, by biome (§7). V1 fills `defaut` only. Colours are token names of constants/rawColors.ts, the one place hex lives in the app. `decors` and `eau` give the piece family (the folder part of the image key, pieces.ts) and the colours of the vector ground under the pieces; lot 2 may add families per biome.

variantes._doc: Ground variants and decals, drawn in the vector tiles (solVarie.ts). Every cell draws one colour per ground kind, picked by a hash of its coordinates and `graine`, weighted by `poids`; another biome gives other colours and another seed. `decals` are small inked shapes on a few cells (`chance` inside, `chanceBord` within 1 cell of the island edge or a path); `surChemin` lets a decal stand on the path. `bordChemin` is the pebble colour on a grass cell that touches the path (`galet`: its half-axes and ink width in dp), each decal has its own ink width `trait` (0 draws solid shapes with no outline), `assombri` the ink laid over cells 1, 2 and 3 cells from the island edge. `tache` is the size in cells of the soft patches of the lawn and the path: a grid of that period holds a smooth value noise that picks the variant (the variant lists run from dark to light), the per-cell hash only nudges it.

monde._doc: The world around the island (L6-T10, monde.ts), drawn once by the app in map space behind the island: the forest of three species and rocks. It covers the whole frame: an iso view looks down on the ground and has no sky (T23). `graine` fixes every tile (no randomness: the world is the same on every visit). Colours are tokens of rawColors.ts; `voile` and `voileNul` are the night's veil, fixed to the frame's edges.

pointsAccroche._doc: Where season and event decor lands on a stage (§7). Each stage's .anchor.json export holds `pointsAccroche` in two forms: `px` (sprite pixels, origin at the sprite's top left, points [x, y]) and `grid` (grid units from the footprint's back corner, points [gx, gy, z]). `faite`, `porte` and `cheminee` are null on a stage without that part (forge rough has no door, the sails have no point at all); `avantToits` lists the eave points, empty without a roof. Schema only: the values come with each stage's exports, from `blender`; components/village/iso/isoSpec.ts types them (PointsAccroche). Beside `px` and `grid`, `pointsAccroche` also holds `foyer` ({px, grid, demiLargeur}: top-face middle of the `fire` volume, else the largest `ember`, half-width in px; null without a hearth) and `fenetres` ([{px, grid, largeur, hauteur, face}]: the lit panes the camera sees, size in px, face `gauche` = wall facing +gy, `droite` = facing +gx). Same px convention as the other points (sprite top left); subtract `anchor` for footprint-relative.

couches._doc: Draw order of one building, bottom to top. `decorSaison` is reserved right above the sprite and below the effects, empty in V1.

fenetresSansMur._doc: Windows of a stage's attach points (constants/isoAccroches.json, by index) the painting has no wall for: the app lights none there. Empty since T38: forge_grand's window 2 is re-exported on its lit part (scripts/iso/exports/accroches.py visible()).

socle._doc: L3-T01 (H1): the painted sprites do not carry the building's own shadow on its socle's top; the app draws it (ombres.ts ombreSocle, in the biome's `socleOmbre`) over the sprite, on the socle only. `dejaPeinte` lists the painted images that carry that shadow already: the app draws none over them. Empty since iter 4 (H3-15): the day sprites carry none. Keys are image names (isoSpec `nomImage`).

batiments._doc: The 21 buildings of db/schema.ts buildingCodes. Tier 3 has two stages (T3_MAX_LEVEL). `emprise` (footprint in cells, [along gx, along gy]) is copied from scripts/iso/exports/heights.json by L0-T03; __tests__/iso-layout.test.ts fails if the two disagree. `repere` names what makes the building recognisable at 30 % zoom, by its visible parts (checklist item 7), validated by Guillaume at H0.
